{{infobox football tournament season |title= [[Copa del Rey]] |year= 2020–21 |other_title= |image= |imagesize= |caption= |country= Spain |date= 11 November 2020 – 17 April 2021 |num_teams= 126 |champions=[[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] |count = 31 |runner-up=[[Athletic Bilbao]] |matches= 127 |goals= 345 |top goal scorer= [[Sergio León]] (5 goals) |prevseason= [[2019–20 Copa del Rey|2019–20]] |nextseason= [[2021–22 Copa del Rey|2021–22]] }} The '''2020–21 Copa del Rey''' was the 119th staging of the [[Copa del Rey]] (including two seasons where two rival editions were played). The winners were assured a place in the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa League#Group stage|2021–22 UEFA Europa League group stage]]. Both the winners and the runners-up qualified for the four-team [[2022 Supercopa de España]]. [[Real Sociedad]] were the defending champions, having won the postponed [[2020 Copa del Rey final|final of the previous edition]], which was held two weeks before the [[2021 Copa del Rey final|2021 final]].{{cite news |url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2021/01/28/official-the-copa-del-rey-2019-20-final-set-for-april-3/ |title=Official: The Copa del Rey 2019-20 final set for April 3 |publisher=Athletic Bilbao |date=29 January 2021}} They were already eliminated by [[Real Betis]] in the round of 16 of the 2020–21 edition, before the previous final had been played. Barcelona won the [[2021 Copa del Rey final|final]] 4–0 against [[Athletic Bilbao]] for a record-extending 31st Copa del Rey title.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56779320|title=Lionel Messi scores twice as Barca win Copa del Rey final|website=BBC Sport|date=17 April 2021|access-date=17 April 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/17/messi-stars-as-barcelona-thrash-athletic-bilbao-to-lift-copa-del-rey |title=Messi stars as Barcelona thrash Athletic Bilbao to lift Copa del Rey|first=Sid|last=Lowe|work=The Guardian|date=17 April 2021|access-date=17 April 2021}} As across Spain, match times up to 25 October 2020 and from 28 March 2021 were [[Central European Summer Time|CEST]] ([[UTC+02:00|UTC+2]]). |attendance= |referee=Cristian Sánchez Moraga }} ;Notes {{notelist}} ==First round== The first round was played by all the qualified teams, except for the four participants of the [[2021 Supercopa de España]]. The ten winners from the previous preliminary round were paired with ten teams from [[2020–21 La Liga|La Liga]]. The remaining six teams and the 22 teams of the [[2020–21 Segunda División|Segunda División]] were paired with the four [[2020 Copa Federación de España|Copa Federación]] semi-finalists, the fourteen teams that competed in the [[2020–21 Tercera División|Tercera División]] and ten teams from [[2020–21 Segunda División B|Segunda B]]. Finally, the remaining 36 teams from [[2020–21 Segunda División B|Segunda B]] were paired between them. In the case of opponents from the same division, the home advantage was decided by whichever team was drawn first; otherwise, the match was held in the stadium of the lower division team. A total of 56 games were played, with 112 participating teams, from 15 to 30 December 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.rfef.es/sites/default/files/pdf/circular_27_2021_copa_del_rey.pdf|publisher=RFEF|date=13 November 2020|language=es|title=Circular nº 27, Campeonato de España / Copa de S.
